scope: Editorial questions and suggested first reading paths for the twelve core papers. Source-bound setup and claim links are reading aids, not new mathematical or formal assessments.

paper-i.question: How many starting vectors do we need to generate a space under a fixed family of operators?
paper-i.contribution: For a fixed operator action, seed rank counts the generators needed. Complete packet coordinates then reconstruct vectors and operators from their components, connecting generation, relations and transfer blocks.
paper-i.limits: The single-operator count assumes finite dimension over the declared field. Infinite reconstruction retains the stated topology and convergence assumptions.

paper-ii.question: How do packet coordinates and operator transfers change when we refine the scale?
paper-ii.contribution: The paper gives coherent coordinate changes across refinement levels, exact formulas for refined operator blocks, weighted path inverses and integral precision bounds.
paper-ii.limits: Refinement uses complete idempotent systems. Infinite path inverses require the stated filtered completeness; contour constructions retain their admissible-contour assumptions.

paper-iii.question: How can packet coordinates describe nonlinear maps and expose failures of transport or correction?
paper-iii.contribution: Complete finite packets give exact coordinates for nonlinear maps. The paper develops composition, derivatives and correction obstructions, with separate hypotheses for smooth transport and convergent expansions.
paper-iii.limits: Exact coordinate reconstruction requires a complete packet system. Differentiability, convergence and Hilbert-space assumptions enter their respective results; the finite formal core covers only part of the manuscript.

paper-iv.question: What can we learn by splitting an analytic function into residue classes of its coefficients?
paper-iv.contribution: Cyclic projections organize differential cycles, reciprocal coefficients and addition laws. For the specified cyclic analytic family, the paper also develops zero geometry, products and coefficient asymptotics.
paper-iv.limits: The analytic conclusions concern this declared family. Complex powers require either a formal-series interpretation or a chosen logarithm on a suitable zero-free domain.

paper-v.question: How can we split, filter and reconstruct a signal while keeping track of every channel?
paper-v.contribution: Residue projectors turn signals into exact polyphase channels and filters into transfer matrices. The same analysis–synthesis language describes perfect reconstruction, finite-depth Haar transforms and edge-packet calculations.
paper-v.limits: Infinite signal results retain their specified sequence space and norm. Exact known-edge reconstruction assumes the edge packet is supplied; estimated packets have separate error bounds.

paper-vi.question: How do evolution, averaging and conditioning behave when a system is viewed through packets?
paper-vi.contribution: Transfer blocks express semigroup composition through intermediate packets. Refinement defects quantify disagreement between coarse and fine evolution, with stochastic, Bayesian and analytic realizations.
paper-vi.limits: Finite-state, positivity and operator assumptions belong to their individual results. Gap-dependent estimates retain their common-gap hypothesis; the finite formal contract has a narrower scope than the manuscript.

paper-vii.question: What can quantum states, symmetries and channels reveal when we resolve them into operator packets?
paper-vii.contribution: The finite theory studies seed generation, symmetry projectors, circuit paths, measurement and channel blocks. Further chapters develop geometric and continuum research directions with their own stated obligations.
paper-vii.limits: The finite algebraic and Hilbert-space hypotheses remain attached to each result. The five physical continuum targets are open; the inherited finite formal items do not certify the entire book.

paper-viii.question: How can an operator be compiled into packet blocks while preserving its exact action?
paper-viii.contribution: Packet layouts give exact evaluation and composition rules, together with operation and storage counts for declared block structures. The paper separates these semantics from numerical and GPU realization questions.
paper-viii.limits: Exact identities use the stated matrix and layout assumptions. The inherited formal contract excludes numerical QR/SVD and canonical singular-value API identification; GPU execution was not performed.

paper-ix.question: How can residue packets and precision towers organize arithmetic sequences and local lifting?
paper-ix.contribution: The paper develops exact coefficient reconstruction, coordinate transport, valuation estimates and lifting constructions. Its later arithmetic results retain their individual field, ring and precision hypotheses.
paper-ix.limits: Finite residue reconstruction is over a declared commutative ring. Broader extensions and the ordinary Euler-tail simplicity endpoint remain open; formal evidence covers selected developments.

paper-x.question: What can lifting a residual representation recover, and which existence questions remain beyond it?
paper-x.contribution: Residual classes form separate lifting branches. The paper studies reconstruction along those branches and conditional completion in supplied compatible carriers, separating vertical lifting from horizontal existence.
paper-x.limits: Completion depends on the declared comparison, carrier and occupancy inputs. Transported targets and a summand in a supplied carrier are distinct outputs; general arithmetic attachment remains open.

paper-xi.question: Which finite pieces of arithmetic representation data can be reconstructed, and what comparison inputs are still needed?
paper-xi.contribution: The paper resolves finite monodromy, Frobenius and character packets and develops restricted comparison constructions. It separates those finite results from the general arithmetic realization problem.
paper-xi.limits: Each comparison retains its stated tame, wild and coefficient hypotheses. General arithmetic realization is Conjecture 66, and the full comparison of pair local factors remains conditional.

paper-xii.question: How does deformation support lead to Hecke occupancy, and which inputs make arithmetic completion possible?
paper-xii.contribution: The paper develops algebraic support descent, finite Hecke packet decompositions and conditional completion criteria. It distinguishes a point being supported from the additional arithmetic data needed for automorphy.
paper-xii.limits: Support results retain their finiteness and Noetherian assumptions where stated. Arithmetic completion requires explicit occupancy, comparison and classicality inputs; universal companion existence is not proved.
